items.title: Invertible equals locally free of rank one when the local rings are local
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file modules.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a locally free module of rank one is invertible, and conversely that an invertible module is locally free of rank one when all local rings are local, the converse failing in general (author lemma at source lines 4376-4382, label lemma-invertible-is-locally-free-rank-1). The proof (source lines 4384-4415) first records a one point counterexample for the parenthetical, then proves that a locally free module of rank one is invertible because the evaluation map is an isomorphism over a trivialising covering, and finally proves the converse by classifying invertible modules over a local ring and upgrading freeness of the stalks to local freeness through finite presentation (proof lines 4385-4414). The converse with its classification step is the content. H2.
